newsitem.title: USA: Two U.S. executives charged with bilking models.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. executives charged with bilking models.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday it filed fraud charges against two New York executives who allegedly stole $1.2 million from several top fashion models.

Peter Bucchieri and David Weil were the president and chief executive officer of Star Capital Management Inc., a New York firm that provided investment advice and business management services to about 30 clients, most of them models.

The SEC did not name the models. Wayne Carlin, an SEC attorney handling the case, said the models worked for Elite Model Management, the New York modelling agency ranked as the largest in the business.
Bucchieri, 40, and Weil, 33, were charged in a civil complaint filed in a federal court in Manhattan.
The SEC said that Weil sought and obtained in most cases complete control over the clients' finances, including bank accounts.
They diverted their clients' money to fund Star's operations, pay for personal expenses and, in one case, to use as collateral for a loan to buy a Porsche car, the SEC said.

The two executives were not registered as investment advisers, in violation of SEC regulations. Weil falsely described himself to prospective clients as a "millionaire former investment banker," the SEC said.
A lawyer representing Weil was not immediately available to comment. Bucchieri's lawyer could not be reached.
Star was incorporated in Colorado in 1992 and went out of business in April 1995, the SEC said.
